sections.skill: Check generated diagrams, maps and charts against real data

questions.prompt: Do image generators check facts when they draw a map?

choices.text: No; they make pictures that look like maps
Yes; every generated map is checked against official satellite data before it is shown

questions.correct_answer: No; they make pictures that look like maps
questions.intro: Image generators make pictures that LOOK like diagrams, maps and charts, but they do not check facts or measure data. A generated map may place cities in the wrong spots or invent roads; a chart may have bars whose heights do not match their labels; a science diagram may label the wrong part. For anything meant to INFORM, build the diagram from real data or a trusted source, for example with a spreadsheet chart or an official map, or check every label, number and position against that source. Use generated images for decoration, not as evidence.

sections.skill: Check a chart against its numbers

questions.prompt: A = 5, B = 10, C = 15. Which bar should be tallest?

choices.text: A, because the first bar in a chart is always drawn as the tallest one

questions.intro: To check a bar chart, compare each bar's HEIGHT with its NUMBER. The biggest number should have the tallest bar, the smallest number the shortest, and a number twice as large should look about twice as tall. Also read the AXIS: does it start at 0? Example: bars labeled A = 5, B = 10, C = 15. C should be tallest, A shortest, and B about twice A. If B is drawn shorter than A, the chart is wrong.

sections.skill: Spot subtle chart and diagram errors

questions.prompt: A chart's axis starts at 50, so 52 looks twice as tall as 51. What is the problem?
questions.intro: Some errors are subtle. A chart's axis may start at 50 instead of 0, making small differences look huge. A diagram may be mostly right but swap two labels. A map may have the right shape but the wrong scale. Read axes and legends, count items, and compare with the source. If you use a generated picture as an illustration next to real data, label it clearly as an illustration so readers do not treat it as accurate.
